title: 3D Shape Dissection: Dehn Invariant and Hilbert's Third Problem
description: Formalizes the Dehn invariant approach to Hilbert's Third Problem: proves the cube has zero Dehn invariant (rational angles) while the tetrahedron has nonzero invariant (irrational angle), showing they cannot be scissors congruent.

meta.author: Dehn (1900), Sydler (1965)

mathlibDependencies.description: Positivity of arccos for angle bounds

originalContributions: Simplified Dehn invariant: dehnInvariantZero predicate via rational angle test
cube_dehn_zero: cube has zero Dehn invariant (π/2 = (1/2)π)
tetrahedron_dehn_nonzero: tetrahedron has nonzero Dehn invariant
dehn_obstruction: cube and tetrahedron have different Dehn invariants
polygon_dehn_zero: 2D Bolyai-Gerwien analog (all polygons have zero Dehn invariant)
Comprehensive documentation: Hilbert's 3rd problem, Dehn-Sydler theorem, dimension contrast

references.citation: Dehn, M., Ueber den Rauminhalt, Mathematische Annalen 55 (1900), 465-478.
Sydler, J.-P., Conditions nécessaires et suffisantes pour l'équivalence des polyèdres de l'espace euclidien à trois dimensions, Comment. Math. Helv. 40 (1965), 43-80.

sections.title: Scissors Congruence
sections.summary: Defines ScissorsCongruent and proves reflexivity and symmetry.

sections.title: Dihedral Angles
sections.summary: Defines cube (π/2) and tetrahedron (arccos(1/3)) dihedral angles. Proves cube angle is rational multiple of π.

sections.title: Dehn Invariant
sections.summary: Defines dehnInvariantZero predicate. Proves cube has zero and tetrahedron has nonzero Dehn invariant.

sections.title: Hilbert's Third Problem
sections.summary: States Hilbert's 3rd problem and dehn_obstruction theorem.

sections.title: 2D Contrast (Bolyai-Gerwien)
sections.summary: Proves polygon_dehn_zero: all 2D shapes have zero Dehn invariant.

conclusion.summary: Formalizes the Dehn invariant approach to scissors congruence with 3 sorries, 0 axioms. Key proved: cube_dehn_zero, tetrahedron_dehn_nonzero (modulo angle irrationality), dehn_obstruction, polygon_dehn_zero.
conclusion.implications: Provides a machine-checked formalization of Hilbert's Third Problem via the Dehn invariant, demonstrating that equal-volume polyhedra need not be scissors congruent — unlike the 2D case (Bolyai-Gerwien theorem).
openQuestions: Prove tetrahedron_angle_irrational_pi (Niven's theorem: arccos(1/3)/π is irrational)
Formalize the full tensor product Dehn invariant in ℝ ⊗_ℤ (ℝ/πℤ)
